paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: your words and your habits are never small. Solomon fills this chapter with pictures of fools, slackers and gossips, and none of them are flattering (Proverbs 26:1-28). Then he points to someone with even less hope than a fool: "Do you see a man who is wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him." (Proverbs 26:12). The slacker gets a similar line, because he is "wiser in his own eyes than seven men who answer discreetly." (Proverbs 26:16).

So what do we do with it? Solomon says guard your mouth, because words are like fire. "Without wood, a fire goes out; without gossip, a conflict ceases." (Proverbs 26:20). Saying "I was only joking!" doesn't put the arrows back (Proverbs 26:18-19). And I think the sneakiest trouble is the hateful man who disguises himself with his speech (Proverbs 26:24), because "When he speaks graciously, do not believe him…" (Proverbs 26:25). Friend, you and I get to be the ones who pause before we speak, and I need that reminder as much as you do.

Solomon also says a hateful man's concealed wickedness "will be exposed in the assembly." (Proverbs 26:26), and that "He who digs a pit will fall into it, and he who rolls a stone will have it roll back on him." (Proverbs 26:27). That's why the wise take a good look at their own hearts first. The wise ask for help, listen to correction, and keep their words honest. That's the kind of baker I want in my kitchen, and it's the kind of baker I'm excited to help you become.
